scenario_text: A gas flows steadily through a smoothly narrowing then widening duct that includes a throat. The local flow speed relative to the local sound speed varies along the duct, and this ratio governs whether the flow accelerates or decelerates as the cross-section changes. For fixed reservoir conditions we evaluate the local Mach ratio as a function of area ratio in the subsonic branch.

The candidate retains this classical core (the isentropic area-Mach term). However, it adds numerous composite correction terms that are NOT part of any textbook formula: (1) a wall-friction correction Cf*Ar*log(Ar)*M^2/(1+(gam-1)/2*M^2) representing accumulated Fanno-type drag along the duct with an unusual Ar*log(Ar) area dependence; (2) a diabatic heat-addition term (Qh0 + Qh1*(Tw/T0-1))*(gam-1)*M^2*(1+gam*M^2)/(1+(gam-1)/2*M^2)^2 that couples wall-temperature-dependent heat exchange (Rayleigh-type) with a temperature-sensitivity coefficient; (3) a Reynolds/pressure-gradient coupling term -Cf*Kre*(pback/p0-1)*Ar*M^3/(...)^((3*gam-1)/(2*(gam-1))) representing boundary-layer growth response; and (4) a separation blockage correction with a tanh switching function Csep*Ar*M^2*(...)*(1+tanh(Ksep*(pback/p0-1-Msep*(1-M^2)))) modeling adverse-pressure-gradient-induced separation. While the individual physical concepts (Fanno flow, Rayleigh flow, boundary-layer separation) are each classically known, no textbook presents them combined into this single implicit equation with these specific composite functional forms (e.g., Ar*log(Ar), the tanh separation onset with Msep*(1-M^2) residual dynamic head argument, the specific exponent combinations). Therefore the equation, taken as a complete combined form, exhibits genuine novelty beyond the classical baseline.
